title: A skeleton of $\Dctf$ is a set of compact generators
statement: Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\ge1$, $q=p^a$, a field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ with $q$ elements, and an algebraic closure $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of $k_0$, the global finite-field datum of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$. Let $X$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k$, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] ([def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism]). Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. The admissible commutative condensed coefficient rings $\Lambda$ here are: the condensation of a finite discrete commutative ring $A$ annihilated by a power of $\ell$; the condensations of $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E$ with their $\ell$-adic topologies [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]; and the ring $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}}_\ell$ of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], whose sections on a profinite set $S$ are the continuous maps $S\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with image contained in one finite subextension. Write $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]; in the last case this is exactly [def-sfb-qlbar-coefficient-ring]. Write $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ for the module-object category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and put $\mathcal T=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$, its ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All small sets and coproducts use [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)\subseteq\mathcal T$ be the bounded constructible finite-Tor-amplitude category [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. In this statement $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$ is the full subcategory of this fixed $\mathcal T$ obtained by intersecting all full replete triangulated subcategories [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory] containing $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ and closed under its ambient small coproducts, as in [det-def-localizing-closure-existence](2). Let $G$ be a small skeleton of $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, that is, a set of representatives of its isomorphism classes. Every object of $G$ is compact [def-pc-compact-object] in $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$. If $K\in\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$ satisfies $\Hom(C[n],K)=0$ for every $C\in G$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$ (shifts as in [def-weil-triangulated-category]), then $K$ is isomorphic to the zero object.

proof.text: For a finite admissible coefficient ring $\Lambda=A$, [det-ctf-finite-compact-proetale] states that every $C\in\Dctf(X,A)$ is compact in $\Loc(\Dctf(X,A))$. Every object of the given skeleton $G$ belongs to this category, so this proves compactness in the finite case.

Finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ gives a finite affine cover by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Its pairwise intersections are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-open-intersection], since $X/k$ is separated. They are quasi-compact, so [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion](2) makes $X$ qcqs. For $\Lambda=E$ or $\underline{\Qlb}$, [sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit](4) gives $\Dctf=\Dbc$. Their localizing closures are therefore equal by the intersection definition in [det-def-localizing-closure-existence](2). By [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums](3), this closure is contained in $\Dic$, defined by cohomology sheaves that are filtered colimits of constructible sheaves. Both nodes use the same condensed $E$ and finite-subextension-valued $\Qlb$ rings as the statement. For $C\in G$ and a small family $(K_i)$ in the closure, apply the explicit canonical-map assertion of [sk-thm-constructible-compactness]. Its hypotheses hold: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ with the fixed finite-field datum, $\ell\ne p$, $X/k$ separated of finite type, $C\in\Dbc$, and $K_i\in\Dic$. Its finite constant local-model constructibility and ordinary ambient category $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ also agree. Thus $\bigoplus_i\Hom(C,K_i)\to\Hom(C,\bigoplus_iK_i)$ is an isomorphism in this ambient category. Fullness identifies the Hom groups with those of the closure, and [det-def-localizing-closure-existence](1)-(2) identifies its coproducts with the ambient ones. This proves compactness. Taking $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ includes that case.

For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, clause (2) of [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc], with $X$ qcqs by step 2, gives $\Dctf=\Dbc$ and equality of their localizing closures for this fixed coefficient ring. The current statement of [det-prop-int-compactness-compact] uses $R_X=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ and the ordinary unbounded category $D(\Mod_{R_X})$, exactly the coefficient object and ambient category fixed here. The preamble identifies $\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ with its valuation-topology condensation, so the identification fixes the ring object before taking its module category. Its standing hypotheses are our prime $\ell$, field $k$ of characteristic $p\ne\ell$, separated finite-type $X/k$, and finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Its abbreviations $\Dbc$ and $\Loc(\Dbc)$ therefore mean $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and the same full localizing closure. Clause (3) asserts that for every small family $(K_\alpha)$ in this closure, the canonical map $\bigoplus_\alpha\Hom(C,K_\alpha)\to\Hom(C,\bigoplus_\alpha K_\alpha)$ is an isomorphism for every $C\in\Dbc$. Apply this to each $C\in G$: by the preceding equality $C\in\Dbc$, and the canonical map is exactly its compactness map in the required closure. No derived-completeness condition or completed coproduct is introduced. Ambient coproducts and the localizing closure are supplied by [det-def-localizing-closure-existence](1)-(2). Taking $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ gives $\mathcal O_E=\mathbf Z_\ell$. Together with steps 1-2, these exhaust the admissible coefficients.

Put $\mathcal L=\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$, and fix $K\in\mathcal L$ with the stated vanishing. For exactly the condensed ring $\Lambda$ in the statement, clauses (1)-(2) of [det-def-localizing-closure-existence] supply the ambient coproducts and the full replete localizing subcategory $\mathcal L$ inside $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$. Let $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal L$ be the full subcategory on objects $M$ such that every map $M[n]\to K$ is zero for every integer $n$. It contains zero, is closed under isomorphisms and under positive and negative shifts ($M[r]\in\mathcal L$ as $\mathcal L$ is triangulated, and replace $n$ by $n+r$), and contains $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$: for each such $M$, choose an isomorphism $M\cong C$ with $C\in G$ and precompose with its shifted inverse.

Let $U\xrightarrow{u}V\xrightarrow{v}W\xrightarrow{w}U[1]$ be a distinguished triangle with $U,V\in\mathcal S$, fix $n\in\mathbf Z$, and let $a:W[n]\to K$. If $n\ge0$, apply TR2 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] $3n$ times; if $n<0$, use its reverse implication $-3n$ times. This gives the distinguished triangle with vertices $U[n],V[n],W[n]$ and arrows $\varepsilon u[n],\varepsilon v[n],\varepsilon w[n]$, where $\varepsilon=(-1)^n$. Since $V\in\mathcal S$, the composite $a\circ(\varepsilon v[n])$ is zero. Clause (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact] supplies $b:U[n+1]\to K$ with $a=b\circ(\varepsilon w[n])$. But $U\in\mathcal S$ gives $b=0$, so $a=0$. Moreover $W\in\mathcal L$: by TR2 the rotation $V\to W\to U[1]\to V[1]$ is distinguished, $V,U[1]\in\mathcal L$, and $\mathcal L$ is a full replete triangulated subcategory [det-def-localizing-closure-existence](2), so $W$ is isomorphic to an object of $\mathcal L$ and lies in $\mathcal L$. Thus $W\in\mathcal S$. To check the middle-object closure in the definition of a triangulated subcategory, if $U,W\in\mathcal S$, reverse rotation gives the distinguished triangle $W[-1]\to U\to V\to W$. Its first two objects lie in $\mathcal S$ by shift closure, so the cone closure just proved gives $V\in\mathcal S$ (here $V\in\mathcal L$ directly by the middle-object clause for $\mathcal L$).

source.place: Tag 0149, lemma-representable-homological (contravariant assertion); rotations from Tag 0145, definition-triangulated-category (TR2). Expands Generation in sk-lem-brown-hypotheses-generation.proof.md.

proof.text: Let $(M_i)_{i\in I}$ be any small family in $\mathcal S$. Its ambient coproduct $M=\bigoplus_i M_i$ exists and belongs to $\mathcal L$ by [det-def-localizing-closure-existence](1)-(2). For any integer $n$, the inverse shift equivalence of [def-weil-triangulated-category] identifies maps $M[n]\to K$ with maps $M\to K[-n]$. The universal property of the coproduct identifies these with families of maps $M_i\to K[-n]$, equivalently maps $M_i[n]\to K$. Each component is zero, so the original map is zero. This includes the empty coproduct. Therefore $\mathcal S$ is closed under arbitrary small direct sums.

By steps 4-6, $\mathcal S$, viewed as a full subcategory of $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$, is closed under isomorphisms, shifts, cones and arbitrary small direct sums and contains $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$. Clause (2) of [det-def-localizing-closure-existence], applied to this fixed ring and this class of generators, gives $\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal S$. In particular $K\in\mathcal S$, so at $n=0$ one has $1_K=0$. The zero maps $K\to0$ and $0\to K$ are then inverse: their composite on $K$ is $0=1_K$, and their composite on the zero object is its unique endomorphism. Thus $K$ is isomorphic to the zero object.

tool_uses.why: Generic theorem for ANY condensed ring: provides the localizing closure, ambient sums and minimality for the exact chapter coefficient object, without importing sk-def-localizing-closure's conflicting Qbar coefficient convention.
Definition of compactness used in the statement; it introduces no alternate proof route.
Generic shift equivalence and TR1-TR3 axioms used to prove cone closure explicitly; the unit does not restate these axioms.
Clause (2) for the integral coefficient ring O_E only, as required by the unit compactness step; no Qbar coefficient change is taken from this statement.

Only its explicit rational ctf=Dbc assertion (4) is used for the chapter coefficient objects; the same identification prescribed by the Brown unit, without deriving ambient compactness from a 2-colimit.

Clause (3) places the generically defined rational localizing closure in Dic with the exact current condensed coefficients, so the displayed Hom/direct-sum assertion in the unit-prescribed rational compactness theorem applies without using its stale closure-definition reference.
